children.text: In the extraordinary year of 1988 in the Arcadian Calendar, we find ourselves at an even more extraordinary weekend. Next Monday, we will welcome a brand-new station director, as well as a brand-new name. Here and now, I wish to take a moment with everyone to look back on this TV station's 120-year history, and look forward to everything we are about to experience.

One hundred and twenty years ago, our entire network consisted of a single program called the "Arcadian Morning Report," operating on the sole philosophy of delivering 24-hour non-stop news coverage. Today, thanks to the tireless efforts of generations of employees, we have left an indelible mark on arcadia, not just through our news reporting, but through our comprehensive entertainment planning. Seafeld TV is always changing; the only constant is our pursuit of change itself.
We live in an age of attention. I think everyone would agree that

, which has captured the avid attention of the entire arcadia, has revitalized the TV station from top to bottom. It goes without saying that Director Fulwish is at the very center of this storm of attention; by using her name as our brand, we can further reshape the market and leave a deeper, more lasting impression on the entire arcadia.

Director Fulwish says that in this fast-paced era, media professionals must be like the Aether Network. have to learn to move at lightspeed. Our station has a long history, and that's exactly why it needs a shot in the arm. This applies both internally and externally. We need to adopt the inventor mentality of the Punklordians: never stop learning, never stop creating. Through constant change, we can keep a firm grip on the pulse of the times.

Our success has only just begun, but don't take it for granted. We are writing history here, and our future knows no limits. Everyone has the chance to help build a brand-new, stylish, and dynamic Fulwish TV.
Starting next week, let's create more happiness for our arcadia... and more Elation.
Assistant and Secretary of the Station Director
